Time gaps require timestamps for each interaction occurrence. Keep ordered `(item, timestamp)` pairs, select identical history indices, truncate both arrays together, and left-pad both with a shared validity mask. Training timestamps align with input events; next-item labels shift separately. Inference requires the same alignment for the supplied history. The official [TiSASRec sampler/evaluator](https://github.com/JiachengLi1995/TiSASRec/blob/master/util.py) demonstrates this paired construction. Consequently, item IDs alone cannot recover elapsed times: repeated items have distinct occurrence timestamps, and even identical item sequences can have different gaps. An item→timestamp lookup is insufficient; sequence-only inference needs an unambiguous external occurrence mapping or an interface extension.

[2Gated-TimeGRU](https://aisel.aisnet.org/hicss-57/da/data_science/10/) explicitly adds consecutive-interaction intervals. The authors’ [related 2TGRU description, equations 5–9](https://doi.org/10.21203/rs.3.rs-3713146/v1) uses learned transformations of `log(t_j−t_{j−1}+γ)` and `log(t_{j+1}−t_j+ε)`, followed by sigmoid gates; γ and ε are learned. This is not a documented fixed exponential decay. The future-gap gate additionally requires a prediction-time timestamp at the final step. That description does not specify timestamp units, missing/first-gap policies, temporal normalization, or decay/gate initialization. Separately, TiSASRec documents per-user minimum-positive-gap normalization, fallback scale 1 when all gaps are zero, and clipped interval indices; these are not 2TGRU defaults.

For this benchmark, prioritize the BPR-max-only GRU trial if aligned inference timestamps are unavailable. Any temporal variant needs explicit, checkpointed choices for units, scaling, missing gaps, truncation boundaries and initialization; padding must not create artificial elapsed time, and unknown gaps must not silently become observed zero gaps. Never substitute a held-out target timestamp for an unavailable prediction time.
